description: This circular chart, likely from the paper "MMAR A Challenging Benchmark for Deep Reasoning in Speech, Audio, Music, and Their Mix," presents a hierarchical breakdown of analysis layers and their constituent components. The chart is structured with a central ring labeled "Perception" and an outer ring labeled "Content Analysis," both divided into segments. The "Perception" ring, colored in a medium blue, contains several components including "Music Theory," "Counting & Statistics," "Environmental Perception & Reasoning," "Correlation Analysis," "Temporal Analysis," and "Spatial Analysis," each occupying a distinct segment without explicit percentage labels. The "Content Analysis" ring, in a lighter blue, is divided into "Semantic Layer (41.2%)" and "Cultural Layer (14.1%)" with the "Semantic Layer" being the largest segment. The "Cultural Layer" is further subdivided into "Professional Knowl & Reasoning," "Culture of Speaker," "Imagination," "Acoustic Quality Analysis," "Anomaly Detection," and "Audio Difference Analysis," each with a distinct segment. The chart includes a legend-like structure with labels pointing to each segment, and the percentages are explicitly shown for the "Semantic Layer" and "Cultural Layer." The chart does not appear to have exploded or emphasized segments, and the segments are arranged in a clockwise order, with the largest segments (Semantic Layer and Content Analysis) occupying the majority of the chart's area.
